A.explanation: Moving $12 \text{ cm}$ across three antinode spacings gives $\lambda = 0.080 \text{ m}$, so $f = 330/0.080 \approx 4100 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: This uses only two $\lambda/2$ spacings for $12 \text{ cm}$, giving $\lambda = 0.060 \text{ m}$ instead of three spacings.

C.explanation: This treats the $12 \text{ cm}$ as $1.5\lambda$, confusing antinode spacing $\lambda/2$ with node-to-antinode spacing $\lambda/4$.

D.explanation: This treats $12 \text{ cm}$ as $4 \times \lambda/2$, counting four intervals instead of the three intervals between first and fourth maxima.

hints: Notice that maximum loudness means an antinode of the stationary sound wave, where the two identical waves reinforce.
Recall that adjacent antinodes are $\lambda/2$ apart, and count how many such gaps lie between the first and the fourth maximum.
Convert the $12 \text{ cm}$ move to metres and combine $v = f\lambda$ with $330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $f$.
walkthrough: Maximum loudness occurs at an antinode, so the microphone starts at one antinode and stops at the third antinode along from it.
From first to fourth maximum there are $4-1 = 3$ antinode-to-antinode gaps, each of width $\lambda/2$.
Rounded to two significant figures this is about $4100 \text{ Hz}$. This is option A.
